components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 0.4375rem; background: oklch(0.55 0.12 52); color: oklch(0.993 0.003 92); font-family: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.48 0.11 51.5); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.55 0.12 52 / 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Offset Workspace Plaque
components.description: The one straight-on flat dark workspace tablet that carries the landing's product proof.
components.css: .ds-workspace-plaque { position: relative; width: min(100%, 420px); aspect-ratio: 1.82; margin: 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(241,239,234,.38); border-radius: clamp(18px, 1.5vw, 26px); background: #1a1918; box-shadow: 0 18px 32px -18px rgba(10,9,8,.28), 0 38px 72px -48px rgba(10,9,8,.48); } .ds-workspace-plaque::after { position: absolute; z-index: 2; inset: 4px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08); border-radius: calc(clamp(18px, 1.5vw, 26px) - 4px); pointer-events: none; content: ""; } .ds-workspace-screen { display: flex; height: calc(100% - clamp(14px, 1.44vw, 24px)); margin: clamp(7px, .72vw, 12px); flex-direction: column; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 4px; padding: 20px; overflow: hidden; border-radius: clamp(11px, .8vw, 16px); background: linear-gradient(180deg, #191818 0%, #151414 52%, #121111 100%); color: #f1efec; font-family: "Hanken Grotesk", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-workspace-screen span { font-family: "Satoshi", "Hanken Grotesk", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 22px; font-weight: 300; } .ds-workspace-screen small { color: #9fb4d4; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
Not the cliché architect loft with mood boards and espresso — a working drawing office where sheets are pinned, dimensions are checked, and decisions leave marks. SiteWise fuses two shipping visual dialects: the standalone Offset Project Monolith landing and the product cockpit workbench. The landing is a warm sheet that lets one dark workspace tablet do the physical work; operate surfaces are dense IBM Plex UI, warm paper greys, micro-radii for finger targets, and a charcoal shell with subtle grain. The shared soul is material clarity, spatial hierarchy, and one purposeful action colour against quiet hardware.

The technology undertone is structural, not neon. On the landing, the evidence is the real Seven Hills workspace capture, framed as a straight-on flat tablet with a thin bezel, inset hairline and diffuse shadow; in product it is carried by registration-tick corners and tracked mono labels. The system is never purple glow or chatbot chrome. Hope is earned by a legible project state.

The landing is a single static Persuade composition for D&C project directors and design managers delivering $5m–$50m projects: left reading column, right straight-on tablet, and graphite project plane naming the synthetic Seven Hills Townhouse demonstration.
keyCharacteristics: Dual-register system: Offset Project Monolith landing vs workbench product, one brand spine
Warm ivory and graphite on landing; Formwork Ember / Blueprint Azure remain product signals
Satoshi + Hanken Grotesk for landing; IBM Plex for operate body
One right-hand straight-on workspace tablet replaces feature-grid or chapter-spine marketing
The landing's Open Datum mark and blue CTA are intentionally landing-only
Tonal stack + restrained lift in the app; a flat tablet and graphite plane on landing

rules.name: The One Hot Accent Rule
rules.body: Product operates with Formwork Ember; this standalone landing operates with Landing Blue. Keep each surface to its one hot voice — never competing accent chrome.

rules.name: The Evidence vs Inference Rule
rules.body: Blaze/ember marks evidenced or brand-owned actions; Blueprint Azure marks AI/assumed/info. Do not swap those meanings.

rules.name: The Paper Before Paint Rule
rules.body: Most of the UI is warm grey paper or charcoal plate. Color arrives as signal, not decoration.

rules.name: The Eyebrow is Structure Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked mono labels are frame, not decoration. Keep them faint with an optional ember tick — never loud pill soup.

rules.name: The Dual Face Rule
rules.body: Satoshi/Hanken Grotesk own the standalone landing; IBM Plex owns operate. Crossing faces needs intent, not drift.

rules.name: The Monolith vs Bench Rule
rules.body: The landing earns attention through one offset workspace machine and a graphite plane; product stays on the tonal workbench. Do not turn dense operating views into landing composition.

rules.name: The One Machine Rule
rules.body: The landing's flat tablet is allowed one diffuse shadow treatment because it contains the product proof. Do not spread that lift across copy, controls or new cards.

rules.name: The Lift Is Earned Rule
rules.body: In product, shadows mark floating or interactive chrome. Surfaces at rest stay tonal.

rules.name: The Mark Is Landing-Only Rule
rules.body: The Open Datum mark belongs to this static landing; it does not authorise a global navigation or app-logo change.

dos: Do use the landing's warm sheet, one straight-on flat workspace tablet and graphite project plane as a single composition.
Do keep Landing Blue rare and purposeful on the landing; keep Formwork Ember purposeful in product.
Do use Blueprint Azure for inference/AI/info and ember for evidenced/brand.
Do use the supplied Seven Hills screenshot as labelled synthetic product demonstration, not customer proof.
Do synthesise and reduce — architect clarity over dashboard clutter.
donts: Don't run purple/indigo “AI” gradients, glow stacks, or chatbot-bubble aesthetics.
Don't add Signal Orange, Formwork Ember or a second hot accent to the current landing composition.
Don't turn the landing into a feature-card grid, chapter scroller or sticky presentation.
Don't distribute the machine's grounded shadow to copy or generic marketing cards.
Don't invent testimonials, partner proof, or metric theatre without real evidence (product constraint).
